report:
**Conclusion:** The claim is broadly supported, but the evidence shows a *modest average improvement in depressive symptoms*, not proof that anti-cytokine drugs are established antidepressants.

A systematic review/meta-analysis of seven placebo-controlled trials (2,370 participants) in chronic inflammatory conditions found anti-cytokine treatment improved depressive symptoms versus placebo (standardized mean difference 0.40—small to moderate). The treatments were being used for the inflammatory disease; depression was usually a secondary outcome, so this does not establish treatment efficacy for diagnosed major depressive disorder.  
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27752078/

The effect may be partly indirect. Less pain, fatigue, disability, and inflammatory disease activity can improve mood; separating these benefits from a direct brain/cytokine antidepressant effect is difficult. The review nevertheless reported that the association was not fully explained by physical-illness improvement, though those analyses were limited.  
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5794896/

A later patient-level “mega-analysis” pooled 18 randomized placebo-controlled trials and standardized symptom measurement across studies, a stronger design for checking consistency. It included follow-up at 4–16 weeks, but assessed depressive *symptoms* using general scales (SF-36 or HADS), rather than enrolling people for clinical depression. Thus it strengthens evidence of symptom benefit during immunomodulatory treatment, while leaving uncertainty about which drug, disease, or patient subgroup benefits most.  
https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7244402/

**Bottom line:** For people with chronic inflammatory disorders who have depressive symptoms, anti-cytokine treatment can modestly reduce those symptoms—especially while effectively treating the underlying disease. It should not currently be viewed as a standalone depression treatment or a replacement for evidence-based depression assessment, psychotherapy, and/or antidepressant treatment when indicated.
